title: Holds Before Stadiums
bigQuestion: How do we know people wrestled long before there were leagues, clocks and weight classes?

story.title: Stone Wrestlers in Athens
story.kicker: A carved stone in a museum is far older than any gym clock.
paragraphs: In Athens, Greece, a block of white marble sits in the National Archaeological Museum. It was carved around 510 BCE. That is about 2,500 years ago. Once it held up a statue over a grave.
In 1922, workers found the block inside an old city wall of Athens. People long ago had reused it as a building stone. The wall kept its carvings safe for many centuries.
One side of the block shows young athletes. In the middle, two wrestlers face each other. A young man stands at each side and watches. The carver cut every arm and leg with care.
The scene has no clock on the wall. It has no scale for weighing people. It has no league name and no printed bracket. Those things came much later, over the last two hundred years.

Stones like this one help historians. They show that wrestling is very old. They also show that its rooms and rules have changed many times. Other old pictures and figures of wrestlers survive from Egypt, Mesopotamia and China.
story.think: What can a carving tell us about a sport, and what can it not tell us?

lessons.title: The Walls of Beni Hasan
lessons.mainIdea: Tomb paintings at Beni Hasan in Egypt show hundreds of pairs of wrestlers from about 4,000 years ago.
reading: Beni Hasan is a place on the east bank of the Nile River in Egypt. Local leaders were buried there in tombs cut into a cliff. Many of these tombs date to Egypt's *Middle Kingdom*. That time lasted from about 2000 to 1700 BCE.

Painters covered the tomb walls with scenes of life. Some walls show wrestlers in long rows. There are hundreds of pairs in all. Each pair is painted in a different position, one after another, like frames in a comic strip.

These paintings are *primary sources*. A primary source is something made at the time being studied. The Beni Hasan walls prove that Egyptians knew wrestling well. They do not tell us the rules the wrestlers followed.

words.d: a time in ancient Egypt, about 2000 to 1700 BCE
things made at the time being studied, like paintings, letters or programs
a room or grave where a person is buried

look.title: Rows on a Tomb Wall
look.text: Picture a long wall inside a cliff tomb in Egypt. Row after row of painted pairs stretch across it. Each pair is a little different from the one before. Some men are painted in darker colors and some in lighter colors, so you can tell the two apart.
look.prompt: Why might a painter make two wrestlers different colors?

check.q: Where are the Beni Hasan tombs?
choices: in Egypt, by the Nile River
check.why: Beni Hasan is on the east bank of the Nile River in Egypt.

check.q: What is a primary source?
choices: something made at the time being studied
a book written this year about old times
the first page of a textbook
check.why: A primary source was made at the time being studied, like the Beni Hasan paintings.

check.q: What can the Beni Hasan paintings NOT tell us?
choices: the exact rules the wrestlers used
check.why: The paintings show wrestlers but do not write down their rules.

lessons.title: A Story From Mesopotamia
lessons.mainIdea: The Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest written stories, tells of two heroes who wrestle and then become friends.
reading: *Mesopotamia* is the old name for the land between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers. Today most of it is in Iraq. People there wrote on clay tablets. They pressed marks into wet clay with a reed.

One famous story from there is the *Epic of Gilgamesh*. Gilgamesh was a king of the city of Uruk. In the story, he meets a wild man named Enkidu. The two wrestle in a doorway. After the match, they become best friends.

The Epic is a story, not a sports report. We cannot tell whether the match happened. Still, it shows that wrestling mattered to its writers. Many copies were found in the ruins of Nineveh, in a library of King Ashurbanipal.

words.d: the old name for the land between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, mostly in Iraq today
a very old story from Mesopotamia about King Gilgamesh of Uruk
a flat piece of clay with writing pressed into it

look.title: Gilgamesh Meets Enkidu
look.text: Enkidu blocks the door so the king cannot pass. The two grab each other and wrestle like wild bulls. They shake the doorway and the wall. When the match ends, they become friends.
look.cite: The Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet II (Standard Babylonian version)
look.prompt: What happens between Gilgamesh and Enkidu after they wrestle?

check.q: Who wrestles Gilgamesh in the Epic?
check.why: In the Epic, Gilgamesh wrestles the wild man Enkidu. Uruk is his city.

check.q: What did people in Mesopotamia write on?
check.why: They pressed marks into wet clay tablets with a reed.

check.q: Why is the Epic called a story and not a sports report?
choices: It has no people in it.
We cannot tell whether the match really happened.
check.why: The Epic is a story. It shows wrestling mattered, but it does not prove a real match.

lessons.title: The Palaestra and Olympia
lessons.mainIdea: Greek boys trained in a building called a palaestra, and wrestling joined the Olympic Games in 708 BCE, by ancient count.
reading: In ancient Greece, many cities had a *palaestra*. It was a building with an open, sandy yard in the middle. Rooms for washing and oiling the body lined the sides. Boys and young men trained there with a teacher.

The Olympic Games were held at Olympia every four years. Ancient writers said they began in 776 BCE with one footrace. Wrestling was added in 708 BCE, by the same ancient count. It was the first contest there that was not a race.

The Greek word for wrestling was *pale*. The name palaestra comes from it. At Olympia, only free Greek men and boys could compete. Enslaved people could not enter. Married women were not allowed to watch.

words.d: a Greek building with a sandy yard where people trained for wrestling
the ancient Greek word for wrestling
the place in Greece where the ancient Olympic Games were held

look.title: Early Contests at Olympia
look.cite: Ancient Olympic victor lists, as reported by Pausanias, Description of Greece, book 5
look.prompt: Which contest was added first after the footraces? How many years after the first footrace?

check.q: What was a palaestra?
choices: a Greek building for wrestling training
check.why: A palaestra was a Greek building with a sandy yard for training.

check.q: When was wrestling added at Olympia, by the ancient count?
check.why: Ancient writers said wrestling joined the Games in 708 BCE. 776 BCE was the first footrace.

check.q: Who could NOT compete at ancient Olympia?
check.why: Only free Greek men and boys could enter. Enslaved people were shut out.

lessons.title: Milo and the Missing Clock
lessons.mainIdea: Milo of Croton won Olympic wrestling six times, in a sport with no weight classes and no time limit.
reading: *Milo of Croton* is the most famous wrestler of ancient Greece. Croton was a Greek city in southern Italy. Milo lived in the 500s BCE. Ancient writers say he won at Olympia six times, once as a boy.

Greek wrestling had no *weight classes*. A weight class is a group of people close in body weight. At Olympia, a small man could be matched with a very big one. Big, strong men often won for that reason.

Greek wrestling also had no clock. Ancient writers say a wrestler needed three falls to win. A match lasted until that happened. Later tales made Milo seem larger than life. Historians treat those tales as legends.

words.d: a Greek wrestler of the 500s BCE who won at Olympia six times
groups that match people who are close in body weight
an old story told as true that cannot be proven

look.title: An Ancient Travel Writer on Milo
look.text: Milo of Croton won six times at Olympia in wrestling, one of them among the boys. At Pytho he won six times among the men and once among the boys.
look.cite: Pausanias, Description of Greece, book 6 (about 150 CE)
look.prompt: Pausanias lived long after Milo. How might that change how much we trust his count?

check.q: Where was Croton?
check.why: Croton was a Greek city in southern Italy.

check.q: What is a weight class?
choices: a group of people close in body weight
check.why: A weight class matches people who are close in weight. Greek wrestling had none.

check.q: How did an ancient Greek match end, say ancient writers?
check.why: Ancient writers say a wrestler needed three falls. There was no clock.

lessons.title: Bökh at Naadam
lessons.mainIdea: In Mongolia, wrestling called bökh is one of the three games of the Naadam festival each July.
reading: In *Mongolia*, wrestling is called *bökh*. It is one of the country's best-loved sports. It is part of the big summer festival called *Naadam*. The national Naadam opens in the capital, Ulaanbaatar, on July 11.

Naadam has three main games: wrestling, horse racing and archery. People often call them the three games of men. Today women and girls compete in the archery and girls ride in the horse races. Wrestling at Naadam is for men.

Bökh has no weight classes. Winners earn titles, such as Falcon, Elephant, Lion and Titan. A story says the wrestling jacket is open at the chest because a woman once won in disguise. That story is a legend. In 2010, UNESCO listed Naadam as world heritage.

words.d: Mongolian wrestling
Mongolia's summer festival of wrestling, horse racing and archery
a country in East Asia between Russia and China

look.title: Two Rooms for Wrestling
look.text: Room one: a grass field in Ulaanbaatar in July. Hundreds of wrestlers take part. There are no weight classes. A champion earns a title like Lion. Room two: a school gym in winter. Wrestlers weigh in first. Each one wrestles only people in the same weight class.
look.prompt: Name two ways these rooms are different. Which one is older?

check.q: What is bökh?
check.why: Bökh is the Mongolian word for wrestling.

check.q: What are the three games of Naadam?
check.why: Naadam has wrestling, horse racing and archery.

check.q: Why is the open jacket story called a legend?
choices: It is in a rule book.
check.why: A legend is an old story told as true that cannot be proven.

lessons.title: Oil Wrestling at Kırkpınar
lessons.mainIdea: Turkey's Kırkpınar oil wrestling festival, near Edirne, is held every summer and traces its start to the 1300s.
reading: In Turkey, one old style is *oil wrestling*. Wrestlers cover their bodies with olive oil before a match. They wear heavy leather trousers called *kispet*. The oil makes the match slippery.

The most famous oil wrestling festival is *Kırkpınar*. It is held each summer near the city of Edirne, in northwest Turkey. Its organizers say it began in the 1300s, in the time of the Ottoman Empire. That start date comes from tradition.

The winner at Kırkpınar is named başpehlivan, which means chief wrestler. A gold belt goes to the champion. In 2010, UNESCO listed the Kırkpınar festival as world heritage. The same year, it listed Mongolia's Naadam.

words.d: a Turkish style in which wrestlers cover themselves with olive oil
heavy leather trousers worn in Turkish oil wrestling
a famous yearly oil wrestling festival near Edirne, Turkey

look.title: A Date From Tradition
look.text: A festival says it began in the 1300s. Few written records survive from that first year. The date is passed down by the people who run it and the town that hosts it. A school record, like a state champion list, is written down in the year it happens.
look.prompt: How is a date from tradition different from a date in a written record?

check.q: What do Turkish oil wrestlers wear?
choices: a jacket that is open at the chest
check.why: Oil wrestlers wear heavy leather trousers called kispet.

check.q: Near which city is Kırkpınar held?
check.why: Kırkpınar is held near Edirne, in northwest Turkey.

check.q: What does başpehlivan mean?
check.why: Başpehlivan is the title of the Kırkpınar champion. It means chief wrestler.

lessons.title: The Akhara in India
lessons.mainIdea: In India and Pakistan, kushti wrestlers train in an akhara, a pit of soft earth led by a teacher called a guru.
reading: In India and Pakistan, an old style of wrestling is called *kushti*. Another name is pehlwani. A wrestler is called a pehlwan. The style grew from older Indian wrestling mixed with Persian wrestling.
Kushti wrestlers train in an *akhara*. An akhara is a training place with a pit of soft, dug earth. Wrestlers often live and eat together there. A teacher, called a *guru*, leads the akhara.

Many akharas still run today, in cities like Varanasi. Kushti wrestlers also moved onto modern mats. In 1952, K. D. Jadhav won a wrestling bronze at the Helsinki Olympics. It was independent India's first Olympic medal won by one person.

words.d: a style of wrestling from India and Pakistan, also called pehlwani
a kushti training place with a pit of soft earth
a teacher who leads students, such as the head of an akhara

look.title: Earth or Mat?
look.text: An akhara floor is soft earth, dug and mixed by hand. An Olympic floor is a thick foam mat with a circle painted on it. K. D. Jadhav came from the first kind of room. In 1952, he won a medal in the second kind.
look.prompt: What changes when a wrestler moves from an earth pit to a mat with a painted circle?

check.q: What is an akhara?
choices: a kushti training place with soft earth
check.why: An akhara is where kushti wrestlers train, on a pit of soft earth.

check.q: Who leads an akhara?
check.why: A teacher called a guru leads the akhara.

check.q: What did K. D. Jadhav win in 1952?
check.why: Jadhav won a wrestling bronze at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics.

lessons.title: Schwingen in Switzerland
lessons.mainIdea: Swiss wrestling, called Schwingen, takes place in a ring of sawdust, and its big national festival crowns a king.
reading: In Switzerland, the old national style of wrestling is called *Schwingen*. It grew among farmers and herders in the Alps. Wrestlers meet in a round ring covered with *sawdust*. The sawdust makes a soft floor outdoors.

Swiss wrestlers wear short trousers made of tough cloth over their clothes. The trousers have a belt. The match is decided inside the sawdust ring. The loser often brushes the sawdust off the winner's back.

The biggest Schwingen event is a national festival held every three years. Its champion earns the title of Schwingerkönig, which means wrestling king. By tradition, the king wins a live bull as a prize.

words.d: the national style of wrestling in Switzerland
tiny wood chips; Swiss wrestlers meet in a ring covered with it

look.title: Sand, Earth and Sawdust
look.text: A Greek palaestra had a yard of sand. An Indian akhara has a pit of dug earth. A Swiss ring is covered with sawdust. Each floor came from what people had close at hand, long before foam mats.
look.prompt: Why might each place use a different soft floor?

check.q: What covers the floor of a Schwingen ring?
check.why: Swiss wrestlers meet in a ring covered with sawdust.

check.q: Among whom did Schwingen grow?
choices: farmers and herders in the Alps
check.why: Schwingen grew among farmers and herders in the Swiss Alps.

check.q: What does the Swiss wrestling king win by tradition?
check.why: By tradition, the Schwingerkönig wins a live bull.

sections.title: The New Room: Clock and Scale

lessons.title: Weight Classes Come to the Olympics
lessons.mainIdea: The modern Olympics had one open wrestling event in 1896, added weight classes in 1904, and added women in 2004.
reading: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896. They had one wrestling event, in *Greco-Roman* style. It had no weight classes. Carl Schuhmann of Germany won it. He also won medals in gymnastics.

In 1904, the Olympics came to St. Louis, Missouri. That year, *freestyle* wrestling joined the Games. It was split into weight classes. All the wrestlers were from the United States. After that, weight classes became normal in Olympic wrestling.

In 1912, national wrestling groups formed a world *federation*. Today it is called United World Wrestling. It writes the rules for Olympic wrestling. Women's wrestling first came to the Olympics in Athens in 2004.

words.d: a modern Olympic wrestling style, named in honor of ancient Greece and Rome
a modern Olympic wrestling style, first in the Olympics in 1904
a group that joins many clubs or countries under one set of rules

look.title: When Styles Joined the Modern Olympics
look.cite: International Olympic Committee, Olympic results records
look.prompt: How many years passed between men's freestyle and women's freestyle?

check.q: Who won the one wrestling event in 1896?
check.why: Carl Schuhmann of Germany won the Greco-Roman event in Athens in 1896.

check.q: Where were the 1904 Olympics held?
check.why: The 1904 Olympics were in St. Louis, where freestyle first appeared.

check.q: When did women's wrestling first come to the Olympics?
check.why: Women's wrestling first appeared in the Olympics in Athens in 2004.

lessons.title: The School Match Clock
lessons.mainIdea: School and college wrestling in the United States runs on a clock, with periods and weight classes set by rule books.
reading: In the United States, school wrestling has its own style. People call it *folkstyle*, or scholastic wrestling. It is different from the Olympic styles. American high schools and colleges use it.

High schools follow rules from the *NFHS*. That stands for the National Federation of State High School Associations. It began in 1920 at a meeting in Chicago. Its rules set three periods of two minutes each. They also set 14 weight classes.

Colleges follow a separate NCAA rule book. A college match has a longer first period, so it runs seven minutes. The first NCAA wrestling championship was held in 1928. The clock, the scale and the bracket are the newest parts of a very old sport.

words.d: the style of wrestling used in American schools and colleges
National Federation of State High School Associations, which writes high school rule books
one timed part of a match

look.title: How Long Is a Match?
look.unit: minutes of match time, regular periods
look.cite: NFHS Wrestling Rules Book; NCAA Wrestling Rules; United World Wrestling International Wrestling Rules
look.prompt: Which rule book gives the longest match? By how many minutes?

check.q: What style do American high schools use?
check.why: American schools and colleges use folkstyle, also called scholastic wrestling.

check.q: Where did the NFHS begin in 1920?
check.why: The NFHS began at a meeting in Chicago in 1920.

check.q: How long is a regular high school match?
check.why: NFHS rules set three periods of two minutes each.
